title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Treasury tribalism
gist: World Gold Council's weekly monitor frames the week around "Treasury tribalism": robust US data revived rate-hike bets and US-Iran tensions escalated, but the dollar's usually tight link to 30-year Treasury yields has broken down even as its 2-year link holds, because markets are pricing higher short rates as tightening credibility and higher long rates as compensation for fiscal and inflation risk, leaving the dollar technically fragile despite elevated yields.

insights.claim: Stronger-than-expected US labour market and business activity data revived rate-hike expectations for the week.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Robust US labor and activity prints keep the rate-hike case alive, a headwind for rate-sensitive assets even as long-end dynamics diverge.
insights.locator: US labour market and business activity data remained robust

insights.claim: Europe saw a rise in inflation and weaker retail sales during the week.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising inflation alongside softening retail sales is a stagflationary cross-current worth tracking for European rate-path risk.
insights.locator: Europe saw a rise in inflation and weaker retail sales

insights.claim: China's manufacturing sector remained under pressure during the week.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Continued manufacturing weakness keeps China stimulus expectations and industrial-commodity demand risk in play.
insights.locator: China's manufacturing sector remained under pressure

insights.claim: Japan's services sector stayed resilient despite weak consumption.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A resilient services sector against weak consumption points to an uneven Japanese recovery that could complicate the Bank of Japan's policy path.

insights.claim: India's Q2 GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year, exceeding expectations.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A beat this large reinforces India as a standout growth economy relative to a weakening China and sluggish Europe.

insights.claim: Escalating US-Iran tensions and fresh sanctions added to geopolitical risk during the week.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Escalating US-Iran tensions is a live geopolitical risk premium to monitor in oil and safe-haven assets like gold.
insights.locator: escalating US-Iran tensions and fresh sanctions

insights.claim: Global equities closed mixed for the week as bond yields rose sharply, the US dollar weakened, and oil prices gained.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising yields with a weakening dollar and mixed equities is an unusual combination that flags cross-asset dislocation rather than a clean risk-on or risk-off week.
insights.locator: Global equities closed mixed as bond yields rose

themes.theme: Treasury Tribalism: the Dollar Decouples from Long Yields

insights.claim: Despite strong US data and elevated Treasury yields, the US dollar's correlation with 30-year Treasury yields has weakened sharply while its correlation with 2-year yields remains intact, because markets appear to read higher short-term rates as a sign of monetary credibility and required tightening, but higher long-term rates as compensation for fiscal and inflation risk.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: This dollar-yield "tribalism" explains why the dollar looks technically precarious even as yields rise, arguing against a mechanical long-dollar trade on rising rates alone.
insights.locator: the dollar's correlation with 30-year Treasury yields has weakened
